The contractor reviews and consolidates the OECD/Sigma diagnostic findings, conducts targeted design assessments to collect operational information required for subsequent WPs, including data feasibility mapping, institutional baseline mapping, planning-budgeting process validation, pilot site readiness assessment, and a digital systems inventory. It redesigns the Strategic Results Framework using a methodology-first, pilot-based approach that accounts for the current limitations of the national development plan. The contractor develops a comprehensive SRF methodology and standards framework designed for the next national planning cycle, conducts a participatory results clarification exercise with a pilot of sectors, and produces a transitional indicator set for the remaining current planning cycle to enable piloting. Deliverables include the Capacity Development and Change Management Strategy, Competency Frameworks and Training Roadmap, Training Modules and Materials, System Stewardship Package, and System Handover and Transition Protocol. WP8: Digital Enablement Design and Procurement-Ready Specifications. It produces the complete technical basis for procuring a digital M&E platform. normalized.description: Description of the Project: Local Governance Reform Programme (LGRP) III The "Multi-Donor Action (EU-BMZ) - Strengthening Capacities and Institutional Readiness of Reform Actors in Palestine" co-financed by the European Union (EU) and the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and implemented by Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH, aims to enhance the institutional capacity, operational effectiveness, and coordination functions of MoFP and PMO ERO as leading entities in national planning and reform management. The Action will support MoFP in its role as the central coordinating body for national planning by enhancing its capacity to embed data-driven policymaking, ensure coherent approaches across line ministries, and improve coordination across all levels of governance. The Palestinian Authority (PA) faces significant institutional and technical challenges in managing, measuring, and demonstrating public sector performance. Monitoring and evaluation (M&E) functions across line ministries and agencies (LMAs) are narrowly defined, fragmented, and largely disconnected from planning and budgeting decisions. Indicators are poorly formulated, feeder data is weak and uncoordinated, and M&E reporting serves administrative compliance rather than evidence-based management. The Strategic Results Framework (SRF), which is the principal instrument for measuring national results delivery, lacks a usable structure, theory of change, and coherent indicator set. No overarching national M&E strategy exists, and data management responsibilities across government institutions remain undefined and unanchored.
